title: introduce-invocation-compressor-and-slo-smartlink
author: Maya Chen
description: Context and motivation: customer incident SUP-881 showed long-tail token cost spikes correlated with repeated redundant context blocks across streaming and non-streaming invocations. This PR introduces an invocation compression middleware (server-side) that detects repeated prefix patterns at the invocation level and compresses the outgoing trace/metric payloads and token-cost annotations for storage and dashboarding. In parallel, we add a small SLO SmartLink feature that binds compressed invocation fingerprints to SLO incidents so on-call can quickly jump from an SLO violation to representative uncompressed traces for triage. Design notes: the compressor runs in the observability sidecar and performs a lightweight rolling hash to identify repeated prefix segments and a canonical token-map delta encoding to preserve cost attribution per token. Compression is lossless for cost attribution metadata and lossy for raw token text (we store a digest to rehydrate only for on-demand debug flows). The SLO SmartLink stores a compact fingerprint index in the observability metadata service and surfaces a deterministic link in the SLO UI that will trigger a gated rehydration flow and time-bound audit access. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind 'invocation_compressor' and 'slo_smartlink' feature flags; rollout strategy is staged by tenant percentage with a background backfill job to compress 7 days of recent invocations for opt-in tenants. Backfill is throttled and can be paused via the console. Observability impacts: compression reduces storage and query egress for invocation artifacts (estimated ~3x reduction for customers with high prefix reuse). We add new metrics invocation_compressor.compress_rate, invocation_compressor.rehydrate_latency, and slo_smartlink.link_resolution_time; dashboards included in this PR. Testing: unit tests for the rolling hash and delta encoding, integration tests exercising end-to-end compression and rehydration, plus a small replaybench scenario with synthetic repeated prompts. Performance: compressor introduces sub-millisecond overhead on p95 invocation path in production profile; profiling results included in commits. Rollout notes: start at 5% tenants, monitor compress_rate and rehydrate_latency, escalate abort on >100ms rehydrate p95 or if cost attribution divergence >0.1% on sample prompts. Related work: follows patterns in ENG-3421 (token-cost attribution) and complements the token-heatmap panels. Checklist: add feature flags, add metrics and dashboards, add backfill job, e2e tests, docs updates, console link wiring, add perf bench.
commits: feat(observability): add invocation-compressor sidecar and rolling-hash matcher
feat(observability): delta-token-map encoder for cost attribution
chore(flags): add invocation_compressor and slo_smartlink feature flags
feat(ui): SLO SmartLink wiring and gated rehydration flow
tests: add unit tests for compressor and integration replaybench
docs: add runbook and rollout guide for invocation compression
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach — can we avoid double-hashing when rehydration is requested? Also question on GC strategy for fingerprint index.

Author(Maya): We cache the last-10k fingerprints in-memory with LRU; added note and test to ensure GC doesn't evict active SLO links. Rehydration flow computes digest only if the fingerprint is missing (no double-hash).
Priya Nair: Need more clarity on security/audit when rehydrating compressed text for on-call — please add KMS/HSM and access audit in docs.

Author(Maya): Added a section in docs/observability/invocation-compression.md describing gated KMS usage and short-lived rehydration tokens; rehydration now requires audit log entry before full-text retrieval.
Samir Patel: Perf numbers look good; one nit on metrics cardinality — invocation_compressor.compress_rate should be tenant-scoped only, not prompt-shape labelled by full prompt.
Author(Maya): Adjusted metrics to tenant and prompt_shape labels only; removed full prompt label to protect PII and control cardinality.
release_notes: Add invocation compression sidecar to reduce observability storage and speed up SLO triage via SmartLinks. Feature is behind feature flags and rolled out staged by tenant. Includes new metrics and dashboards; see docs/observability/invocation-compression.md for operational guidance.
notes_for_oncall: If slo_smartlink shows >1% unresolved links in 10m window, pause backfill and set feature flag to false for affected tenants.
If rehydrate_latency p95 exceeds 100ms, set invocation_compressor to passive and open an incident runbook: observability/invocation-compressor-runbook.md.
Backfill throttle can be controlled from the console under Observability -> Backfill Jobs -> invocation-compress.
Audit: rehydration requires an audit log entry; check audit.logs for entries before granting on-demand full-text access.
